statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The first full hour after the CME reopen confirms rather than changes Monday's read. NQ futures trade near 29,127.75, about 22 points above the 29,105.75 prior settle, with no reopen gap and very thin volume. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,023.18, down 0.98%, inside a 28,875.97-29,151.97 range and roughly 147 points above the session low, while the Dow gained 0.26% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.76%. VIX is 15.85 after a narrow 15.61-16.06 band, WTI is about 85.21 after a 2.35% decline, and the 10-year yield eased around 3.5 basis points to 4.70%. Tail is 8 in the low band because there is no gap, no session-extreme holding and no failed-retracement extension; the weakness is concentrated in memory and semiconductors while five of eight megacaps closed higher. Stress is 42 in the moderate band, reflecting a Tier-1-free Tuesday calendar ahead of Wednesday's combined Core PCE and Nvidia event stack.
recommendation: Descriptive only. A tape that closes well off its lows, diverges from a green Dow and then reopens flat on thin futures volume is behaving as a sector rotation out of memory and semiconductors, not as an index-level breakdown. Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON with a green status for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The flagged danger window spans 13:30Z-14:30Z on 25 August, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. Every forecast hour still maps to EA_ON because the conditional Tail path peaks at 18, below the watch band. Confidence is 85: futures, cash closes, VIX, yields, oil and the calendar are all verified from primary sources, with the only conflict coming from delayed quote pages that were discarded.
headline: Flat CME reopen holds Tail at 8 as Monday's memory-led de-rating stays contained to semiconductors, with a Tier-1-free Tuesday calendar easing Stress to 42 ahead of Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack
body: The defining evidence for this hour is the shape of the futures reopen. NQ is trading near 29,127.75 against a 29,105.75 prior settle, a 0.08% move on a few hundred contracts, with the Dow contract equally flat at plus 0.05%. There is no reopen gap and no directional extension, which is the structural opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail measure is built to detect. Monday's cash session ended the same way: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,023.18, down 0.98%, inside a 28,875.97-29,151.97 range and roughly 147 points above the low, while the S&P 500 lost only 0.28% to 7,652.86 and the Dow gained 0.26% to 53,417.16. That dispersion is the central fact. The decline was concentrated in the memory and semiconductor complex, where Micron fell about 5.8% on reports that Chinese memory supply could reach large US customers, SanDisk lost 6.4%, AMD 3.5%, Intel 3.1% and Broadcom 2.6%, while Nvidia slipped 2.9% in a seventh consecutive down session ahead of Wednesday's report. Against that, five of the eight tracked megacaps closed higher, with Meta up 1.66%, Amazon up 1.33% and Alphabet up 0.94%, while payment names recovered, Visa adding 3.1% and Mastercard 3.3%. An index that falls while its largest non-chip constituents rise is rotating, not breaking. Cross-asset evidence supports the same reading. VIX finished at 15.85 inside a 15.61-16.06 band, a level that does not price a disorderly tape. The 10-year yield eased about 3.5 basis points to 4.70%, still near its 20-month peak of 4.75% but moving down rather than up alongside equity weakness. WTI fell 2.35% to roughly 85.21 and Brent to 92.26 as the United States rolled out its Iran sanctions programme; oil prices remain structurally elevated by the Strait of Hormuz disruption, but Monday's direction removed rather than added an energy-led amplifier. The delayed Finviz cross-asset context agrees within its stated limits, showing NQ, ES and YM all within 0.06% of unchanged and Treasury futures effectively flat, with the caveat that it is latest-session context and not live price-path evidence. Stress at 42 reflects a genuine catalyst stack rather than current disorder. Tuesday carries no Tier-1 release: Barkin at 12:00Z, weekly ADP at 12:15Z, Case-Shiller at 13:00Z, then Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and the Richmond Fed at 14:00Z, a 2-year auction at 17:00Z and Barkin again at 20:00Z. Wednesday is the pressure point, combining Core PCE, the second GDP estimate and Durable Goods at 12:30Z with Nvidia's report after the close, and Jackson Hole with the Fed chair's keynote follows on Friday. Under the published risk definition, event importance and forecast dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence before they raise Tail; Tail rises on observed path evidence. None of that evidence is present. Confidence at 85 reflects futures, cash closes, VIX, yields, oil and the seven-day calendar all verified against primary sources, tempered slightly by two delayed quote pages that returned figures inconsistent with every other source and were discarded.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 23:00Z on 23 August with Tail 9 and Stress 42 as Asian technology repriced the memory-cost story, then eased to a window floor of 7 with Stress 38 through the overnight hours. The first structural peak came in European and early US hours, with Tail 19 and Stress 58 in a trend-down mode at 07:00Z, easing to 11-13 in a mixed mode through the European morning. The window's only non-green slots came around the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode, mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That structure did not persist. From 15:00Z onward Tail collapsed to 13 and then held a 7-10 band for the remainder of the US session while Stress decayed from 54 to 43, which is the signature of an orderly rotation whose directional efficiency faded rather than a path that denied mean reversion. The window closed at 22:00Z with Tail 8, Stress 43 and a normal mode as futures reopened flat.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 8 on the observed flat reopen, lifts to 11 at 00:00Z when the Tokyo and Seoul cash opens reprice memory costs most directly, then eases through the Asian session to the horizon floor of 7 at 05:00Z in the inter-session gap before the European pre-open, which also carries the lowest conditional Stress of 40. The European open and first full hour lift the series to an overnight peak of 12 at 08:00Z, after which it consolidates in a 10-11 band into the US premarket. The horizon peak of 18 falls at 14:00Z, where the first full US cash hour overlaps the Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster, and that hour carries the only event/whipsaw mode in the forecast alongside the horizon's Stress peak of 55. Conditional Tail then decays to 12 by 16:00Z as post-data volatility normally fades, ticks back to 13-14 into the cash close on positioning ahead of Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack, and settles at 9-10 through the CME maintenance halt and the following reopen. No hour reaches the watch threshold of 20, because none of the amplifiers that would justify it has been observed rather than merely scheduled.
